def test_active_non_ssh_change_skips_fresh_ssh_ack(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            paths = self._paths(Path(tmp))
            calls: list[list[str]] = []
            acknowledgements: list[tuple[str, float]] = []
            statuses = [
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
            ]
            with patch.object(
                firewall_apply, "_binary", side_effect=lambda name: f"/usr/bin/{name}"
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply, "inspect_ufw_service", side_effect=statuses
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply,
                "current_ssh_path",
                return_value=SshManagementPath(
                    server_port=22,
                    client_ip="192.168.88.10",
                    client_port=51000,
                    server_ip="192.168.88.46",
                ),
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply.os, "fchown", return_value=None
            ):
                result = apply_local_config(
                    config(),
                    acknowledge=lambda token, expires: acknowledgements.append((token, expires)) or True,
                    paths=paths,
                    runner=self._runner(calls),
                )

            self.assertEqual(result.status, "APPLIED")
            self.assertEqual(acknowledgements, [])
            self.assertFalse(paths.pending_ack.exists())

    def test_active_ssh_port_change_requires_fresh_ssh_ack(self):
        cfg = FirewallConfig(rules=(
            FirewallRule(
                "b" * 32,
                "standard",
                True,
                "ssh deny test",
                direction="input",
                action="deny",
                protocol="tcp",
                dst_ports="22",
            ),
        ))
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            paths = self._paths(Path(tmp))
            calls: list[list[str]] = []
            acknowledgements: list[tuple[str, float]] = []
            statuses = [
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
                SimpleNamespace(detected=True, status="active"),
            ]
            with patch.object(
                firewall_apply, "_binary", side_effect=lambda name: f"/usr/bin/{name}"
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply, "inspect_ufw_service", side_effect=statuses
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply,
                "current_ssh_path",
                return_value=SshManagementPath(
                    server_port=22,
                    client_ip="192.168.88.10",
                    client_port=51000,
                    server_ip="192.168.88.46",
                ),
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply.os, "fchown", return_value=None
            ):
                result = apply_local_config(
                    cfg,
                    acknowledge=lambda token, expires: acknowledgements.append((token, expires)) or True,
                    paths=paths,
                    runner=self._runner(calls),
                )

            self.assertEqual(result.status, "APPLIED")
            self.assertEqual(len(acknowledgements), 1)
            self.assertTrue(acknowledgements[0][0])
            self.assertFalse(paths.pending_ack.exists())

def test_native_ssh_allow_delete_requires_ack_and_rolls_back_when_rejected(self):
        before = "\n".join((
            "Status: active",
            "[ 1] 22/tcp ALLOW IN Anywhere",
        ))
        after = "Status: active\n"
        status_outputs = iter((before, before, before, after))
        calls: list[list[str]] = []

        def runner(args, **kwargs):
            calls.append(list(args))
            if args[-2:] == ["status", "numbered"]:
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0, next(status_outputs), "")
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0, "", "")

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            paths = self._paths(Path(tmp))
            original4 = paths.user4.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            with patch.object(
                firewall_apply, "_binary", side_effect=lambda name: f"/usr/bin/{name}"
            ), patch.object(
                firewall_apply,
                "current_ssh_path",
                return_value=SshManagementPath(
                    server_port=22,
                    client_ip="192.168.88.10",
                    client_port=51000,
                    server_ip="192.168.88.46",
                ),
            ):
                snapshot = list_numbered_ufw_rules(runner=runner)
                result = delete_numbered_ufw_rule(
                    snapshot[0],
                    snapshot=snapshot,
                    acknowledge=lambda token, expires: False,
                    paths=paths,
                    runner=runner,
                )

            self.assertEqual(result.status, "ROLLED_BACK")
            self.assertTrue(result.ssh_ack_required)
            self.assertEqual(paths.user4.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), original4)
            self.assertTrue(any(call[0].endswith("/systemd-run") for call in calls))

- UX po úspěšném smazání se číslovaný seznam znovu zobrazí, takže lze bezpečně uklidit více nativních pravidel bez vytváření druhého firewall editoru.
- SAFETY fresh-SSH token už není vyžadován po každém aktivním Apply. Při zapnutí neaktivního UFW zůstává povinný vždy; při změně aktivního UFW se vyžaduje jen tehdy, když změněná SysApps pravidla mohou matchnout aktuální `SSH_CONNECTION`. Bez SSH runtime kontextu se použijí porty z `sshd -T`; pokud management cestu nelze spolehlivě určit, rozhodnutí je fail-closed a token se vyžádá.
- SAFETY mazání nativního `ALLOW/LIMIT IN` pravidla, které může krýt používaný SSH port, používá stejný cross-session token a předem armovaný rollback `/etc/ufw/user.rules` + `user6.rules`. Nesouvisející delete se po ověření dokončí bez tokenu, ale rollback je i tak armovaný po dobu samotné mutace.

replacements.new: Status: **guarded manual UFW Apply implemented and cross-session ACK physically verified on dev-vm** as SysApps 2.12.0 / Firewall Manager 0.7.0 (2026-11-13). Hub/hourly auto-apply and production/new21 takeover remain disabled. Activation of an inactive UFW always requires one-time `sys_apps ufw <token>` acknowledgement from a different SSH transport; active Apply requires it only when changed managed rules can affect the current SSH management tuple, otherwise the pre-armed rollback is cancelled immediately after successful verification. Native/legacy UFW rules can be listed through `ufw status numbered` and explicitly deleted; an SSH-relevant permissive delete uses the same token+rollback protection. Add/Edit remains exclusively owned by local `firewall.json`.

The acknowledgement command must bypass the normal menu lock, reject the original SSH session, reject non-SSH invocation, and fail after the rollback deadline.
replacements.new: - Manual Apply must preserve unrelated UFW lines, stage/validate deterministic candidates, back up every touched file, arm an independent time-limited rollback before live activation, run UFW dry-run validation and apply atomically. Activation from inactive always requires acknowledgement from a newly opened SSH session through one-time `sys_apps ufw <token>`; active Apply requires that acknowledgement only when changed managed rules may match the current SSH management tuple. Use `SSH_CONNECTION` as the primary live tuple and `sshd -T` ports only as fallback; uncertainty must fail closed to requiring acknowledgement. The acknowledgement command must bypass the normal menu lock, reject the original SSH session, reject non-SSH invocation, and fail after the rollback deadline. Verify candidate hashes before committing local apply state.

replacements.old: - Native UFW rule cleanup is intentionally delete-only: list rules through `ufw status numbered`, never add/edit them from this path, and re-read the complete numbered snapshot immediately before `ufw --force delete <number>`. Any change in numbering/content must fail closed; after delete re-read and verify the expected remaining rule texts.
replacements.new: - Native UFW rule cleanup is intentionally delete-only: list rules through `ufw status numbered`, never add/edit them from this path, and re-read the complete numbered snapshot immediately before `ufw --force delete <number>`. Any change in numbering/content must fail closed; after delete re-read and verify the expected remaining rule texts. Every native delete is wrapped in an independent backup/rollback of `user.rules` and `user6.rules`; deleting a permissive inbound rule that may cover the current SSH management port additionally requires the same fresh-SSH token before rollback cancellation.
